resolutions.researcher_notes: Searched FERC docket CP18-513 context (via the DOE/FERC EA), SEC full-text search (efts.sec.gov) for 'Stage 3 Pipeline'/'CCL Stage 3'/'feed gas pipeline' + 'in service', and Cheniere Corpus Christi Holdings LLC's FY2022/2023/2024 10-Ks (cch-20221231.htm, cch-20231231.htm, cch-20241231.htm) for a current operating-status statement specific to this 21-mile/42-inch Stage 3 pipeline segment. None of the three most recent CCH 10-Ks names a second, distinct in-service pipeline separate from the original 'Corpus Christi Pipeline' (P0373, 48-inch/23-mile, in service 2018) — each year's Item 1/2 business description still speaks of a single ~21-21.5-mile gas supply pipeline. CONCERN: this is worth a human check on whether the Stage 3 Pipeline (docket CP18-513, EA at https://www.energy.gov/sites/prod/files/2019/09/f66/ea-2111-corpus-christi-lng-stage-3-2019-03.pdf) has actually entered commercial service as its own asset, given the EA's own 2019 schedule (line ~1356: 'Construction of the Stage 3 Pipeline would begin in 2020 with an in-service date in 2023') projects 2023, not the sheet's 2022, and no FERC in-service notice or trade-press completion announcement for this specific 21-mile/42-inch line could be located. This is a scheduling/verification gap, not a value change — do not alter Status/StartYear1 off this note alone; a sibling agent or human with FERC eLibrary access should pull Cheniere's affirmative in-service filing in Docket CP18-513-000 to settle the actual date.

DOE/FERC Environmental Assessment for the Corpus Christi Stage 3 Project (Docket CP18-513-000/CP18-512-000, March 2019) describes the Stage 3 Pipeline throughout as a natural gas pipeline: '21 miles of new 42-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline' (p. facilities list, EA text line ~72) that would transport 'natural gas' to the Corpus Christi LNG Terminal. Single source (one federal filing), so medium tier, independent: false — the seed FracTracker/PGJ/Cheniere/EIA citations in the brief all describe the ORIGINAL Corpus Christi Pipeline (P0373, 48-inch/23-mile, 2018 in-service), not this Stage 3 segment, and were ruled inapplicable rather than cited here.

See CONCERN under Status [ref] above (same underlying gap): the only dated schedule found is the March 2019 EA's projection of a 2023 in-service date, which does not support the sheet's 2022. Checked SEC EDGAR full-text search for 'Stage 3 Pipeline'+'in service' (0 hits) and 'Corpus Christi Pipeline Stage III'+'in service' combinations; checked CCH's FY2022-2024 10-Ks for a completion announcement (none specific to this pipeline). Also checked Exhibit 21.1 subsidiary lists across CEI's 10-Ks: 'Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline Stage III, LLC' appears in the FY2015/2016 10-Ks (filed 2016-2017) but is already absent from the FY2021 10-K (filed 2022-02-24) subsidiary list — consistent with an entity merger sometime 2017-2021, but that is a corporate-restructuring date, not a pipeline in-service date, so it cannot be used to support 2022. No REFS_ADDED possible without overclaiming; leaving UNRESOLVED per the brief's rule against proposing a ref that doesn't actually support the value.

Delayed=yes/DelayType=inferred is GEM's own internal inference (comparing an original projected date to actual/current status), not typically something an external source states directly. Same search effort as the Start/Status units above applies; found nothing that independently confirms or dates a schedule slip for this specific segment beyond the EA's own original 2023 target. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than fabricate support for an inferred field.

EA text (line ~1218): the Stage 3 Pipeline Facilities would operate at '1,440 psig and a capacity of approximately 1.5 billion standard cubic feet per day (Bcf/d)' — 1.5 Bcf/d = 1,500 MMcf/d, which is 'approximately' the sheet's 1,530.00 MMcf/d (prose-vs-precise-figure match per the brief's equivalence rule: an EA's rounded 'approximately 1.5 Bcf/d' design capacity is the same design-capacity claim as the sheet's more precise 1,530 MMcf/d). Single source, medium tier, independent: false.

EA text (line ~72, ~700, ~1271): 'CCPL would construct approximately 21 miles of new 42-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline' — 21 miles = 33.8 km, matching the sheet's LengthKnown 33.80 km exactly. Single source, medium tier, independent: false.

EA text repeatedly specifies '42-inch-diameter' for the Stage 3 Pipeline (e.g., line ~72: '21 miles of new 42-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline'; line ~1718: 'The 42-inch-diameter Stage 3 Pipeline would be installed generally parallel to the 48-inch-diameter [existing Corpus Christi Pipeline]' — this last passage also independently confirms the Stage 3 Pipeline is a physically distinct line from the original 48-inch Corpus Christi Pipeline, P0373, not a duplicate of it). Matches sheet's Diameter 42.00 in exactly. Single source, medium tier, independent: false.

EA text: 'The Stage 3 Project would consist of the following facilities in San Patricio County, Texas' and 'the Stage 3 Pipeline Facilities would be located entirely within San Patricio County, Texas.' Confirms Texas/United States for both endpoints (sheet leaves StartLocation/EndLocation/District blank and only asserts State/Country, which this document supports). Single source, medium tier, independent: false.

Both filings are Cheniere/CCH's own SEC disclosures, so this is one origin (the Cheniere corporate family reporting on itself), not two independent publishers -- medium tier, independent: false. Cheniere Corpus Christi Holdings LLC's FY2022 10-K (cch-20221231.htm) states that in June 2022 Cheniere contributed 'Corpus Christi Liquefaction Stage III, LLC ... formerly a wholly owned direct subsidiary of Cheniere' into CCH, where it merged into CCL, 'our wholly owned subsidiary' -- i.e. the entire Stage 3 corporate chain (Cheniere Energy, Inc. -> CCH -> CCL/CCP) is 100% owned, no minority partner, consistent with Owner1=Cheniere Energy 100%. Cheniere Energy Inc.'s FY2016 10-K Exhibit 21.1 (Subsidiaries of the Registrant) separately lists 'Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline Stage III, LLC' as a named subsidiary of the registrant (Cheniere Energy, Inc.) alongside the other Corpus Christi entities, corroborating that the pipeline-specific Stage III entity was also within the wholly-owned Cheniere corporate family before being merged into Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline, L.P. (the entity that ultimately built/owns this pipeline). No source gives an explicit standalone 'X% owned by Cheniere Energy' sentence for the pipeline itself, hence medium not high.
